title: Marianne Fatton and Oriol Cardona Coll win first ski mountaineering Olympic golds
content:
BORMIO, Italy — The first-ever Olympic gold medalists in ski mountaineering are Switzerland’s Marianne Fatton and Spain’s Oriol Cardona Coll.

In the women’s sprint race, Fatton, the two-time world champion, upset the heavy favorite from France, Emily Harrop, who held a significant lead during the early parts of the climb up the Stelvio. But Fatton closed the gap during the first transition, then extended her lead during the second when Harrop had trouble putting her skins away.

After Fatton raced down the hill on her skis and crossed the finish line first in 2 minutes, 59.77 seconds she collapsed in the snow. She’d made history, as the first Olympic champion in her sport’s history.

Ski mountaineering is making its Olympic debut this year, the first new sport to the Winter Games since 1998.

Harrop, the six-time world champion who hadn’t lost a sprint race in nearly a year, was 2.34 seconds back and won silver. Spain’s Ana Alonso Rodriguez took bronze.

American Anna Gibson of Wyoming, competing in just her third and fourth professional ski mountaineering races, entered as the 18th-ranked competitor but advanced to the semifinals before being knocked out.

In the men’s sprint final, the two Swiss competitors, Jon Kistler and Arno Lietha, led throughout the climb, distancing themselves from the pack. But Cardona Coll, the reigning world champion, closed in the first transition and dominated from there, racing away from the field to win in 2:34.03. As he skied down the Stelvio, victory in hand, he raised his poles in triumph. He pumped his fists. He blew kisses to the crowd. He hugged his fellow competitors.

Cardona Coll currently owns the World Cup title, the world championship and now the Olympic gold medal.

Nikita Filippov, a native of Russia competing as a neutral athlete in these Games, took silver after finishing 1.52 seconds back. France’s Thibault Anselmet earned the bronze.
